approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and begins each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its highest-scoring half. A memory keeps the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and its strongest eligible records join the current examples with their original accepted strings and scores. Historical examples receive diminishing weights based on how many earlier fitting batches used them, while the total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. The policy minimizes weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, using up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the final policy. It directly samples complete SMILES, with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refilling each batch.
approach.novelty: Add an individual log-probability ceiling to the fitting targets: replace only positive targets with zero. This removes the positive excess that a normalized sequence model cannot reach while keeping every nonpositive target and the Parent's exposure weights. The earlier shared-normalization sibling shifted every target in an affected batch, reversed some learning directions and lost sequence completion in two replicas. Ceiling projection never turns a capped row toward lower likelihood. The two Huber siblings bounded residual influence symmetrically; this change acts only on targets above the probability ceiling. Same-state target and gradient comparisons will test execution, and later molecular proposals will test utility. Multiple zero targets are still jointly incompatible, and collapsing distinctions among saturated targets can weaken useful exploitation.

hypothesis: Project each selected sequence's augmented likelihood target independently onto the nonpositive log-probability half-line, t_i = min(frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, 0), while preserving the Parent's inverse-exposure historical coefficients, selected membership and squared-residual Adam update.

finding_summary.headline: Ceiling projection changed real learning and reduced duplicate draws, with an uneven gain in final score.
finding_summary.insights:
Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.results:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with uneven attachment chemistry, concentrated analogue families and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-c2ef5c1d5a78 produces substantial organic structures, dominated by aromatic amides, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl sulfonamides and cyclic amines. The digest reports 870 optimizer proposals per task; ring-closure rates range from 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.946 to 0.9931. These are fractions of SMILES strings containing the indicated features, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The passive RDKit audit finds median heavy-atom counts of 24, 33, 28, 24 and 24 in the fixed task order, with median perceived ring counts of 3, 4, 3, 3 and 3. All 4,350 accepted optimizer appearances parse, but parsing is not a synthetic-route or stability assessment. Constitutional exploration is broad: the respective distinct atom-typed Murcko scaffold counts are 540, 356, 588, 733 and 775; these counts also distinguish linker and ring-atom changes and do not establish useful diversity. The strongest subsets can nevertheless concentrate on a single decorated core. Most leading structures have recognizable medicinal chemistry, alongside very flexible, highly aromatic, reactive-handle and unusually assembled outliers. The entire panel has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies 832 optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. Against Parent n-3462511d7ff0, two tasks have identical chemical records, while the others mainly change families or their substitution and linkage patterns. Score-gradient interpretations below are associations within recorded structures, not hidden-objective definitions, activity measurements, causal matched-pair experiments unless stated, or mechanism-activation judgements. All five task trajectories were supplied and read; tasks_without_trajectories is empty in the brief. Descriptor definitions, exact input hashes, Parent comparisons and structural receipts are saved in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-06-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized, aromatic amides: anilides, benzylamides, pyridyl ethers, pyridones and indole carboxamides. The leading seed-2 ether-linked bis-pyridyl anilide has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings; its molecular weight is 319.364. The next benzyl-pyridone/pyridylmethyl benzamide and methylamino diaryl-ether analogue have the same heavy-atom count and molecular weight. These ordinary amide and aryl-ether connections appear makeable, while the low tail includes small inorganic/ionic fragments and elaborate polycycles. The Parent also led with aromatic amides; the node changes their heteroaromatic and linker arrangements. For example, the seed-0 leading family changes from a substituted pyrrole tertiary carboxamide at recorded 0.4902347642636414 to an acetamidoindole benzylamide at 0.43351949803907636. Seed 2 instead reaches the cited ether-linked anilide at 0.5, versus the Parent aromatic amide at 0.4767312946227961.
liabilities: The low tail contains overbuilt fused/bridged polycycles with unspecified stereochemistry; their valid SMILES do not supply a practical synthesis.

A high-scoring O-benzyl hydroxamate-like amide and a sulfinamide illustrate less routine N-O and sulfur attachment chemistry; the latter has an unassigned sulfur centre. These groups require individual assessment and are not inherently invalid.
The final expanded multi-anilide retains substantial aromatic surface and extra amide burden despite its very low score.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the moderate-sized, organized aromatic amide/ether combination during late exploration: expanded amide assemblies and fragmented outputs lose that organization.
Controlled heteroatom placement and linker topology within that composition range remain unresolved; abundant rings do not imply the required arrangement has been found.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading 24-heavy-atom aromatic amides score 0.5 or 0.4767312946227961; the isolated thiocyanate representation scores 5.670115669739515e-23, and the enlarged 44-heavy-atom multi-amide scores 3.2151129360788796e-21. Late growth to the related 35-heavy-atom multi-anilide at seed-2 evaluation 296 gives only 0.00015241757289843227. A moderate size/composition window and specific aromatic nitrogen/amide organization are therefore supported better than indiscriminate ring or amide addition. The differently connected leaders sharing molecular weight still differ in score, so size alone is not sufficient; the records do not identify a unique absent target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are all seed-2 variants of a butoxy/dimethoxy 4-anilino-2-phenylquinazoline, with fluorine/chlorine substitutions and related alkoxy changes. The leading molecule has 35 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings, molecular weight 483.490 and nine rotatable bonds. The aryl-amino and aryl-ether connections are recognizable synthetic chemistry, although heavy decoration increases size and route complexity. Full trajectories also contain other families: a dinitrophenylhydrazone in seed 0 and a nitrogen-rich fused heteroaromatic family in seed 1. Compared with the Parent seed-2 sulfonamide/imine-decorated quinoline leader at 0.6085883514313919, the node reaches the cited quinazoline at 0.6669492630755185. The largest Murcko family grows from 71 Parent proposals to 160 node proposals; this local concentration coexists with 356 distinct node scaffolds.
liabilities: The leading family combines extensive aromatic surface, multiple halogens and flexible alkoxy substituents; solubility, conformation and synthesis remain unmeasured.
The broader stream still includes heavily nitrated hydrazones and large aliphatic ionic outliers. Their presence should not be confused with useful scaffold coverage.
No stereochemistry is specified even in branched alkoxy variants that can carry a stereocentre.
missing_features: The leading excerpt lacks alternative core architectures that retain the successful substituent arrangement: its apparent variety largely comes from decoration of one quinazoline framework.

The local score differences support more precise substituent positioning and ether connectivity, but do not identify any particular unobserved scaffold or missing functional group as the objective answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The strongest decorated quinazoline scores 0.6669492630755185. A difluoroaniline member scores 0.6666996765035981, whereas its same-fluorine-count positional isomer at final evaluation 298 scores 0.6362655153804642. Removing the butoxy oxygen in the cited final analogue gives 0.6316114681166585; these local comparisons support sensitivity to substitution position and linkage. Ring-rich sulfones in the worst excerpt score 0.28535067873303166 and 0.28799019607843135, while a long-chain quaternary ammonium compound scores 0.5. Thus the score is not a general measure of aromatic richness, size, or chemical plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules have accessible non-acylated amines combined with aromatic groups: benzyl/aryl piperazines, benzene-fused azepines connected through aminoalkyl chains, and aryl ketones bearing propoxy-piperidine substituents. The first digest leader has 30 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and a saturated piperazine, with molecular weight 463.463 and calculated TPSA 6.48. The next fused-azepine leader is smaller, at 26 heavy atoms and molecular weight 360.448, but retains a flexible linker. These are recognizable medicinal scaffolds, with conventional amine/aryl chemistry in many examples. The Parent also produced cyclic amines, but its seed-2 near-ceiling leader carried an N-hydroxyaminal connection; the node supplies ketone-linked examples instead. Parent seed-0 recorded best 0.9961294199375436 becomes 0.9999997933663268 for the cited piperazine family; this is chemical comparison at an already compressed score ceiling.
liabilities: The highly aromatic first leader has little calculated polar surface, while other leaders carry long flexible linkers and multiple potentially protonatable amines; neither actual protonation nor solubility was measured.
The chloromethyl ether in a leader scoring 0.9999994163676008 is a reactive attachment requiring scrutiny even though the recorded score is high.
The final polyether-linked amide has 17 rotatable bonds and score 0.5728095677025575, showing that extensive flexible growth is still admitted.
missing_features: Some low and final proposals lose the combination of a non-acylated cyclic amine and the larger aromatic/linker arrangement; the generator can emit these features but does not preserve their chemical roles consistently.
Several high-scoring aminoalkyl families lack linker restraint. More constrained counterparts are a chemical coverage gap, with no demonstrated score benefit from the records supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Free cyclic amines with suitably connected aromatic groups occur repeatedly near the score ceiling. By contrast, the N-sulfonyl piperidine example scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the N-acyl piperidine example 2.6715842904959654e-05: a nitrogen ring whose nitrogen is sulfonylated or acylated is chemically different from a free amine. Late seed-2 ketones retaining the propoxy-piperidine appendage score 0.9999937368364026 and 0.999988872643426, whereas the smaller amino-ketone lacking that appendage scores 0.0035116287191461495. Those are not single-change matched pairs, but support the importance of amine/aryl spacing beyond mere nitrogen presence. The many nearly identical high scores cannot establish a preferred linker length or experimental binding affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules combine aryl sulfonyl groups with piperazine, quinoline or benzodioxole units. The leading molecule is an unsymmetrical bis-sulfonyl piperazine linking a methylquinoline and benzodioxole: 32 heavy atoms, five perceived rings, three aromatic rings and molecular weight 475.548. Other strong examples retain N-methyl or N-aryl piperazines; the broader stream also contains amides and assorted heterocycles. Aryl sulfonamide assembly is recognizable makeable chemistry, whereas the seed-1 N-rich unsaturated ring is less routine. Every supplied node and Parent record agrees in evaluation, source, SMILES and score across all seeds for this task, so there is no molecular-output change to describe.
liabilities: Repeated sulfonyl and piperazine additions can produce large, acceptor-rich molecules without improving on the more compact leader.
The leading bis-sulfonyl piperazine has no free basic piperazine nitrogen; any intended ionization property must follow its actual substitution, not the ring name.
The low tail includes a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide and an organic azide; these are chemically distinct reactive or specialized compounds, not evidence of routine medicinal plausibility.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring proposals lack the combined aromatic/sulfonyl/piperazine organization; isolated amine or sulfonyl motifs do not reproduce the leading arrangement.

A more effective topology beyond the observed bis-sulfonamide is not identifiable from these scores. The enlarged example shows that duplicating recognizable fragments does not resolve that uncertainty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393. The smaller quinoline sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine scores 0.2272296156064184, and the expanded structure carrying additional sulfonyl-piperazine material scores 0.2301209791058402 despite reaching 41 heavy atoms and molecular weight 628.795. Small acyclic compounds, including the cited organic azide at 0.0 and thiodiacetic acid at 0.02095188685475281, lack the combined ring/linker architecture. A late simple pyrrolylmethyl piperazine scores 0.10826206026353223, so piperazine alone is insufficient. Both nitrogens of the leading piperazine are sulfonylated: a missing free basic nitrogen is not supported as this objective's general deficit.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger excerpt remains chemically heterogeneous. It includes a butylamino-acetyl N-acylsulfonamide on a fluoro/trifluoromethyl phenyl ring, a branched oxalamide/anilide, sulfonylated cyclic amidines bearing an aromatic ester, a guanidino benzofused amine, and an acylthiourea quinolinone. The first three leaders have 23, 26 and 25 heavy atoms and molecular weights 356.341, 377.338 and 362.382; the first two each have only one aromatic ring, whereas the cyclic-amidine ester has three rings overall. Several fragments are synthetically familiar, but the varied N-acylsulfonamide, amidine, hydrazone and acylthiourea connections need individual chemical assessment. All supplied node/Parent chemical records and scores are identical across the seeds; this chemistry is inherited unchanged in the observed output.
liabilities: The high-scoring amino-acylsulfonamide combines a potentially basic amine with a potentially acidic N-acylsulfonamide; a neutral SMILES does not establish its solution microstate.
The acylthiourea and sulfonylhydrazone families introduce tautomeric or configurational questions, while the branched oxalamide is explicitly stereochemically undefined.
Large peptide-like and lipid-like outliers carry substantial size or flexibility burdens. The final stream still contains densely carbonylated or imino structures at very low recorded scores.
missing_features: Reliable compact assembly with the local polarity and substituent arrangement seen in the better examples is missing from many proposals; late carbonyl-rich and bulky structures still depart from those arrangements.

The branched oxalamide, guanidino benzofused amine and other chiral proposals lack specified tetrahedral configurations. This is a molecular-definition gap; these trajectories do not test whether stereochemical assignment changes the objective score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact amino-acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 and the branched oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. Within the sulfonylated cyclic-amidine ester family, adding the cited aryl fluorine changes the recorded score from 0.24905607529893223 to 0.3034617343186778. Replacing the methyl ester in the unfluorinated family with an ethyl carboxamide gives 0.20841151065209942. Thus substituent identity and polar-group arrangement matter locally. The large peptide-like structures, extended lipid-like chain and heavily substituted polyaromatic examples in the worst excerpt have zero or extremely small scores. However, unfluorinated guanidino and acylthiourea leaders also score 0.2711448282680827 and 0.26424211308214746. Neither more fluorine nor more rings is a supported universal requirement, and the diverse leaders do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Free cyclic amines recur among near-ceiling molecules, while cited N-acyl and N-sulfonyl versions of nitrogen rings occur at very low scores. Elsewhere the strongest bis-sulfonyl piperazine deliberately has both nitrogens blocked, so no universal free-amine preference is justified. Same-fluorine-count positional isomers on a decorated quinazoline score 0.6666996765035981 and 0.6362655153804642. These examples show why ring names and element counts do not determine chemical function or useful attachment geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator varies atom identities and attachments without consistently preserving the chemical role of the resulting functional group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and explore functional-group roles, atom neighborhoods and substituent positions coherently, including alternatives that preserve a useful arrangement while changing one local connection. Let task-local observed feedback determine which roles matter; impose no universal amine, halogen or scaffold requirement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A 24-heavy-atom aromatic amide scores 0.5, while a related 35-heavy-atom expanded multi-anilide scores 0.00015241757289843227. A 32-heavy-atom bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, while a 41-heavy-atom expanded sulfonyl/piperazine structure scores 0.2301209791058402. Large peptide-like and long-chain outliers also appear at zero or negligible scores. These are observed associations, not universal molecular-size cutoffs.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control size and polar-group growth while retaining the organization of a useful molecular family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support compact additions, removals and replacements that vary size, flexibility and donor/acceptor organization separately enough for feedback to resolve them. Avoid assuming that duplicating a recognized group or increasing ring count preserves the useful whole-molecule arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 12 digest leaders in the decorated anilino-phenylquinazoline basin share that framework, despite extensive fluorine/chlorine and alkoxy variation. Its largest atom-typed Murcko family contains 160 optimizer proposals, versus 71 in the Parent. Across the panel ring-closure rates are already 0.9805 to 0.9966, and many distinct scaffolds occur, so the gap is not an inability to close rings or explore constitutional structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring local exploration can become concentrated on peripheral decorations without demonstrating equivalent access to alternative core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent core and attachment rearrangements alongside decoration changes, retaining substituent roles where possible. Assess resulting molecules through ordinary feedback rather than treating scaffold counts or enforced diversity as evidence of utility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The passive structural audit finds 832 accepted optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. The branched oxalamide scoring 0.3085499097640706 and the sulfinamide scoring 0.4531317717091581 provide digest witnesses. This absence concerns molecular identity, not proven stereochemical sensitivity of the recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no demonstrated ability to specify the stereochemical identities of the chiral molecules it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit stereochemical alternatives when a proposed graph admits them, and preserve assigned configuration through subsequent changes. Keep any usefulness claim conditional on observed feedback; do not assume that stereochemical specification itself improves the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A chloromethyl-ether arylpiperazine has recorded score 0.9999994163676008. The same panel includes an organic azide, a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide, stereochemically unspecified polycycles and amino-acylsulfonamides with competing ionizable groups. All accepted optimizer structures parse, which verifies a narrower property than stability, route feasibility or a defined solution microstate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score-compatible generation still admits reactive attachments and structures whose practical synthesis or solution form is unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain chemically coherent connection types and the ability to distinguish ordinary end-product functionality from reactive handles or unresolved microstates using general chemical context. Treat unusual N-N, N-O and sulfur chemistry individually rather than banning entire bond classes; the observed scores do not substitute for synthetic or physicochemical evidence.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct raw a_i in float32 from each original accepted score and frozen-prior sequence likelihood on the fixed actual training tensor; independently verify t_i=min(a_i,0), exact preservation of every a_i<=0, and removal equal to max(a_i,0). Record positive-target count and positive-excess sum before versus after, by current/history and update phase. Every raw-positive opportunity must have zero actual positive excess; updates without a positive target must retain the exact raw target. Count all-positive unions and logsumexp(t) to expose residual joint inconsistency. On the same policy likelihood and q_i, verify the derivative change is exactly 2*q_i*max(a_i,0), nonpositive targets keep their derivative, and no capped row changes from upward to downward pressure. Float32 arithmetic comparisons allow 1e-6 + 1e-6*max(abs(reference),abs(actual)); exact-control tensor equality is audited separately. Parent scalar audits establish opportunities only, not vector activation.
activation_observables.name: Recompute every selected member's target from its unchanged accepted score and frozen-prior likelihood; record target attainability, target-minus-starting-likelihood sign and the specific target/weight/update change on fixed inputs.

activation_observables.measurement: At identical pre-update parameters and the exact selected tensor, measure actual projected current-only, internally exposure-weighted history-only and count-share combined gradients. Compare the direct actual projected combined gradient to the direct exposure-weighted raw-target comparator on those same members before and after norm-one clipping on detached copies. Use 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(norm_projected,norm_raw) for L2 and orthogonal differences, with cosine only for nonzero norms. Require at least one nonterminal raw-positive residual-bearing opportunity to produce a measurable direction change after clipping; report the full opportunity fraction, scale-only cases, cancellation and near-zero cases without assuming each scalar change must change network direction. The first real unclipped backward must match the projected direct diagnostic within that tolerance, and an actual parameter displacement must be recorded. Target-equal updates are exact same-state gradient controls. finding_summary.headline: Ceiling projection changed real learning and reduced duplicate draws, with an uneven gain in final score.
finding_summary.insights:
Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.results:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

finding_summary.headline: Ceiling projection changed real learning and reduced duplicate draws, with an uneven gain in final score.
finding_summary.insights:
Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.results:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

finding_summary.headline: Ceiling projection changed real learning and reduced duplicate draws, with an uneven gain in final score.
finding_summary.insights:
Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.results:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with uneven attachment chemistry, concentrated analogue families and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Node n-c2ef5c1d5a78 produces substantial organic structures, dominated by aromatic amides, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl sulfonamides and cyclic amines. The digest reports 870 optimizer proposals per task; ring-closure rates range from 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.946 to 0.9931. These are fractions of SMILES strings containing the indicated features, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The passive RDKit audit finds median heavy-atom counts of 24, 33, 28, 24 and 24 in the fixed task order, with median perceived ring counts of 3, 4, 3, 3 and 3. All 4,350 accepted optimizer appearances parse, but parsing is not a synthetic-route or stability assessment. Constitutional exploration is broad: the respective distinct atom-typed Murcko scaffold counts are 540, 356, 588, 733 and 775; these counts also distinguish linker and ring-atom changes and do not establish useful diversity. The strongest subsets can nevertheless concentrate on a single decorated core. Most leading structures have recognizable medicinal chemistry, alongside very flexible, highly aromatic, reactive-handle and unusually assembled outliers. The entire panel has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies 832 optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. Against Parent n-3462511d7ff0, two tasks have identical chemical records, while the others mainly change families or their substitution and linkage patterns. Score-gradient interpretations below are associations within recorded structures, not hidden-objective definitions, activity measurements, causal matched-pair experiments unless stated, or mechanism-activation judgements. All five task trajectories were supplied and read; tasks_without_trajectories is empty in the brief. Descriptor definitions, exact input hashes, Parent comparisons and structural receipts are saved in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-06-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized, aromatic amides: anilides, benzylamides, pyridyl ethers, pyridones and indole carboxamides. The leading seed-2 ether-linked bis-pyridyl anilide has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings; its molecular weight is 319.364. The next benzyl-pyridone/pyridylmethyl benzamide and methylamino diaryl-ether analogue have the same heavy-atom count and molecular weight. These ordinary amide and aryl-ether connections appear makeable, while the low tail includes small inorganic/ionic fragments and elaborate polycycles. The Parent also led with aromatic amides; the node changes their heteroaromatic and linker arrangements. For example, the seed-0 leading family changes from a substituted pyrrole tertiary carboxamide at recorded 0.4902347642636414 to an acetamidoindole benzylamide at 0.43351949803907636. Seed 2 instead reaches the cited ether-linked anilide at 0.5, versus the Parent aromatic amide at 0.4767312946227961.
liabilities: The low tail contains overbuilt fused/bridged polycycles with unspecified stereochemistry; their valid SMILES do not supply a practical synthesis.

A high-scoring O-benzyl hydroxamate-like amide and a sulfinamide illustrate less routine N-O and sulfur attachment chemistry; the latter has an unassigned sulfur centre. These groups require individual assessment and are not inherently invalid.
The final expanded multi-anilide retains substantial aromatic surface and extra amide burden despite its very low score.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the moderate-sized, organized aromatic amide/ether combination during late exploration: expanded amide assemblies and fragmented outputs lose that organization.
Controlled heteroatom placement and linker topology within that composition range remain unresolved; abundant rings do not imply the required arrangement has been found.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules have accessible non-acylated amines combined with aromatic groups: benzyl/aryl piperazines, benzene-fused azepines connected through aminoalkyl chains, and aryl ketones bearing propoxy-piperidine substituents. The chloromethyl ether in a leader scoring 0.9999994163676008 is a reactive attachment requiring scrutiny even though the recorded score is high.
The final polyether-linked amide has 17 rotatable bonds and score 0.5728095677025575, showing that extensive flexible growth is still admitted.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Free cyclic amines with suitably connected aromatic groups occur repeatedly near the score ceiling. By contrast, the N-sulfonyl piperidine example scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the N-acyl piperidine example 2.6715842904959654e-05: a nitrogen ring whose nitrogen is sulfonylated or acylated is chemically different from a free amine. per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules combine aryl sulfonyl groups with piperazine, quinoline or benzodioxole units. The low tail includes a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide and an organic azide; these are chemically distinct reactive or specialized compounds, not evidence of routine medicinal plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger excerpt remains chemically heterogeneous. It includes a butylamino-acetyl N-acylsulfonamide on a fluoro/trifluoromethyl phenyl ring, a branched oxalamide/anilide, sulfonylated cyclic amidines bearing an aromatic ester, a guanidino benzofused amine, and an acylthiourea quinolinone. Large peptide-like and lipid-like outliers carry substantial size or flexibility burdens. The final stream still contains densely carbonylated or imino structures at very low recorded scores.

The branched oxalamide, guanidino benzofused amine and other chiral proposals lack specified tetrahedral configurations. This is a molecular-definition gap; these trajectories do not test whether stereochemical assignment changes the objective score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Free cyclic amines recur among near-ceiling molecules, while cited N-acyl and N-sulfonyl versions of nitrogen rings occur at very low scores. Elsewhere the strongest bis-sulfonyl piperazine deliberately has both nitrogens blocked, so no universal free-amine preference is justified. Same-fluorine-count positional isomers on a decorated quinazoline score 0.6666996765035981 and 0.6362655153804642. These examples show why ring names and element counts do not determine chemical function or useful attachment geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator varies atom identities and attachments without consistently preserving the chemical role of the resulting functional group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and explore functional-group roles, atom neighborhoods and substituent positions coherently, including alternatives that preserve a useful arrangement while changing one local connection. Let task-local observed feedback determine which roles matter; impose no universal amine, halogen or scaffold requirement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A 24-heavy-atom aromatic amide scores 0.5, while a related 35-heavy-atom expanded multi-anilide scores 0.00015241757289843227. A 32-heavy-atom bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, while a 41-heavy-atom expanded sulfonyl/piperazine structure scores 0.2301209791058402. Large peptide-like and long-chain outliers also appear at zero or negligible scores. These are observed associations, not universal molecular-size cutoffs.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control size and polar-group growth while retaining the organization of a useful molecular family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support compact additions, removals and replacements that vary size, flexibility and donor/acceptor organization separately enough for feedback to resolve them. Avoid assuming that duplicating a recognized group or increasing ring count preserves the useful whole-molecule arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 12 digest leaders in the decorated anilino-phenylquinazoline basin share that framework, despite extensive fluorine/chlorine and alkoxy variation. Its largest atom-typed Murcko family contains 160 optimizer proposals, versus 71 in the Parent. Across the panel ring-closure rates are already 0.9805 to 0.9966, and many distinct scaffolds occur, so the gap is not an inability to close rings or explore constitutional structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring local exploration can become concentrated on peripheral decorations without demonstrating equivalent access to alternative core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent core and attachment rearrangements alongside decoration changes, retaining substituent roles where possible. Assess resulting molecules through ordinary feedback rather than treating scaffold counts or enforced diversity as evidence of utility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The passive structural audit finds 832 accepted optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. The branched oxalamide scoring 0.3085499097640706 and the sulfinamide scoring 0.4531317717091581 provide digest witnesses. This absence concerns molecular identity, not proven stereochemical sensitivity of the recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no demonstrated ability to specify the stereochemical identities of the chiral molecules it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit stereochemical alternatives when a proposed graph admits them, and preserve assigned configuration through subsequent changes. Keep any usefulness claim conditional on observed feedback; do not assume that stereochemical specification itself improves the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A chloromethyl-ether arylpiperazine has recorded score 0.9999994163676008. The same panel includes an organic azide, a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide, stereochemically unspecified polycycles and amino-acylsulfonamides with competing ionizable groups. All accepted optimizer structures parse, which verifies a narrower property than stability, route feasibility or a defined solution microstate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score-compatible generation still admits reactive attachments and structures whose practical synthesis or solution form is unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain chemically coherent connection types and the ability to distinguish ordinary end-product functionality from reactive handles or unresolved microstates using general chemical context. Treat unusual N-N, N-O and sulfur chemistry individually rather than banning entire bond classes; the observed scores do not substitute for synthetic or physicochemical evidence.

Lost saturated-target distinctions are a demonstrated limitation, but their causal contribution to the losing seed is unmeasured.

Reducing the same-state scalar factors can weaken exploitation even while improving the final endpoint. One seed loses 0.008594 and mean AUC decreases; this supports uneven utility, without isolating a particular removed molecular feature or optimizer moment as its cause.

Most current rows improve, but 905 historical row residuals worsen and 1,006 historical likelihoods decrease. Shared parameters and persistent Adam can move an individual row away from its target; this does not refute exact scalar target projection.

The molecular assessment retains concentrated analogue families, uncertain attachment chemistry and unspecified stereochemistry. More observed chemical cores and fewer raw duplicates do not consistently align with task score.

Separate group-gradient reductions have small measurable discrepancies from the direct combined diagnostic in 18 child updates. The real backward matches the direct objective exactly, so this qualifies decomposition precision rather than showing a wrong actual objective.

Record positive-target count and positive-excess sum before versus after, by current/history and update phase. Every raw-positive opportunity must have zero actual positive excess; updates without a positive target must retain the exact raw target. Count all-positive unions and logsumexp(t) to expose residual joint inconsistency. On the same policy likelihood and q_i, verify the derivative change is exactly 2*q_i*max(a_i,0), nonpositive targets keep their derivative, and no capped row changes from upward to downward pressure. activation_observables.measurement: At identical pre-update parameters and the exact selected tensor, measure actual projected current-only, internally exposure-weighted history-only and count-share combined gradients. Compare the direct actual projected combined gradient to the direct exposure-weighted raw-target comparator on those same members before and after norm-one clipping on detached copies. Use 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(norm_projected,norm_raw) for L2 and orthogonal differences, with cosine only for nonzero norms. Require at least one nonterminal raw-positive residual-bearing opportunity to produce a measurable direction change after clipping; report the full opportunity fraction, scale-only cases, cancellation and near-zero cases without assuming each scalar change must change network direction. The first real unclipped backward must match the projected direct diagnostic within that tolerance, and an actual parameter displacement must be recorded. Target-equal updates are exact same-state gradient controls. Passive uniform targets use their own ceiling projection and unchanged count state; neither they nor raw-target gradients perform a diagnostic optimizer step.

Reduced projected loss or lower duplication alone does not establish useful molecular improvement.
